scope: Guest Chat native acceptance transport observation
confirmed_cause: The prior acceptance script enabled Network only on the side panel CDP target. The extension sends STREAM_RUN from its service worker to a lazily created offscreen document, where streamFetch issues the AI POST. Chrome target Network events are scoped, so the panel observer recorded zero AI requests even when both answers completed.
repair: Observe the exact extension offscreen target. If it already exists, attach and enable Network directly. If it does not, browser CDP auto-attach pauses new targets and enables Network before resuming. A target with an empty or about:blank initial URL is treated as provisional: only matching POST metadata is buffered until targetInfoChanged confirms the exact offscreen URL; unrelated targets are resumed and their provisional records discarded. No offscreen document is created by the test. A narrowly scoped -32000 response-body unavailable protocol error no longer makes the owned CDP connection fatal; other protocol errors remain fatal. Existing-target detach is verified, and a cleanup failure is recorded separately from an earlier acceptance failure. Each observation retains only attempt, timestamp, CDP request ID, HTTP status, and a syntax-checked structured error code. Opening and follow-up both require a matching request with HTTP status before transport proof can be claimed.
red_proof: The initial scratch-copy mutation disabling offscreen classification failed the first-fetch regression. Fresh peer review then reproduced an empty-initial-URL target with a missed POST; its new test failed with opening_guest_ai_transport_unobserved before repair. The owned CDP test also failed before repair because body-unavailable marked the shared connection fatal.
green_proof: node --test tests/browser/guest-chat-transport-observer.test.mjs tests/browser/guest-chat-store-sequence.test.mjs: 8 passed; node tests/browser/vault-owned-cdp.test.cjs: passed. Coverage includes late target URL, unavailable response body with later request, unrelated protocol error fatality, and verified detach failure. The existing CI test job now runs both commands. Scoped Biome, syntax, and diff checks pass.
limits: No live native browser, hosted acceptance, or CI job execution was performed in this implementer lane; real HTTP status and response code remain unverified until the fresh artifact is exercised.
CDP request ID is a browser-local correlation handle, not a server request ID.
An HTTP error without a structured simple code leaves code null; the HTTP status is still recorded.
